The server keeps ADR-004's warning without blocking the save, so existing content with an empty alt still saves\n- [ ] Tests: the stored Markdown for an insert, the undescribed-image warning still shown, and the existing T10/T11 tests still pass\n- [ ] Browser check recorded in the closing comment: insert, change the description, remove, and the create-page message, each with the browser version, viewport, actions, result, and screenshots\n\n## Blocked by\n\n- #16 (T13)\n\nADR-001-local-admin-static-public.md\nADR-002-stack.md\nADR-003-split-publish-rights.md\nADR-004-chart-images.md\nADR-005-editor-stores-markdown.md\nADR-006-charts-drawn-from-data.md","is_error":false}]},"uuid":"cb0bec60-06b1-4aca-a905-f803efc8b17d","timestamp":"2026-10-01T17:15:07.674Z","toolUseResult":{"stdout":"# Issue tracker: GitHub\n\nIssues and specs for this repo live as GitHub issues. Use the `gh` CLI for all operations.\n\n## Conventions\n\n- **Create an issue**: `gh issue create --title \"...\" --body \"...\"`. Use a heredoc for multi-line bodies.\n- **Read an issue**: `gh issue view <number> --comments`, filtering comments by `jq` and also fetching labels.\n- **List issues**: `gh issue list --state open --json number,title,body,labels,comments --jq '[.[] | {number, title, body, labels: [.labels[].name], comments: [.comments[].body]}]'` with appropriate `--label` and `--state` filters.\n- **Comment on an issue**: `gh issue comment <number> --body \"...\"`\n- **Apply / remove labels**: `gh issue edit <number> --add-label \"...\"` / `--remove-label \"...\"`\n- **Close**: `gh issue close <number> --comment \"...\"`\n\nInfer the repo from `git remote -v`; `gh` does this automatically when run inside a clone.\n\n## Pull requests as a triage surface\n\n**PRs as a request surface: no.** _(Set to `yes` if this repo treats external PRs as feature requests; `/triage` reads this flag.)_\n\nWhen set to `yes`, PRs run through the same labels and states as issues, using the `gh pr` equivalents:\n\n- **Read a PR**: `gh pr view <number> --comments` and `gh pr diff <number>` for the diff.\n- **List external PRs for triage**: `gh pr list --state open --json number,title,body,labels,author,authorAssociation,comments` then keep only `authorAssociation` of `CONTRIBUTOR`, `FIRST_TIME_CONTRIBUTOR`, or `NONE` (drop `OWNER`/`MEMBER`/`COLLABORATOR`).\n- **Comment / label / close**: `gh pr comment`, `gh pr edit --add-label`/`--remove-label`, `gh pr close`.\n\nGitHub shares one number space across issues and PRs, so a bare `#42` may be either: resolve with `gh pr view 42` and fall back to `gh issue view 42`.\n\n## When a skill says \"publish to the issue tracker\"\n\nCreate a GitHub issue.\n\n## When a skill says \"fetch the relevant ticket\"\n\nRun `gh issue view <number> --comments`.\n\n## Wayfinding operations\n\nUsed by `/wayfinder`. The **map** is a single issue with **child** issues as tickets.\n\n- **Map**: a single issue labelled `wayfinder:map`, holding the Notes / Decisions-so-far / Fog body. `gh issue create --label wayfinder:map`.\n- **Child ticket**: an issue linked to the map as a GitHub sub-issue (`gh api` on the sub-issues endpoint). Where sub-issues aren't enabled, add the child to a task list in the map body and put `Part of #<map>` at the top of the child body. Labels: `wayfinder:<type>` (`research`/`prototype`/`grilling`/`task`). Once claimed, the ticket is assigned to the driving dev.\n- **Blocking**: GitHub's **native issue dependencies**, the canonical, UI-visible representation. Add an edge with `gh api --method POST repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<child>/dependencies/blocked_by -F issue_id=<blocker-db-id>`, where `<blocker-db-id>` is the blocker's numeric **database id** (`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<n> --jq .id`, _not_ the `#number` or `node_id`). GitHub reports `issue_dependencies_summary.blocked_by` (open blockers only, the live gate). Where dependencies aren't available, fall back to a `Blocked by: #<n>, #<n>` line at the top of the child body. A ticket is unblocked when every blocker is closed.\n- **Frontier query**: list the map's open children (`gh issue list --state open`, scoped to the map's sub-issues / task list), drop any with an open blocker (`issue_dependencies_summary.blocked_by > 0`, or an open issue in the `Blocked by` line) or an assignee; first in map order wins.\n- **Claim**: `gh issue edit <n> --add-assignee @me`, the session's first write.\n- **Resolve**: `gh issue comment <n> --body \"<answer>\"`, then `gh issue close <n>`, then append a context pointer (gist + link) to the map's Decisions-so-far.\n----\n## Problem Statement\n\nThe office's writers are IR staff and interns, not web developers, but every Data Bite and Report body is typed as Markdown in a plain textarea. A table means lining up pipes by hand, a chart means making it in Excel, exporting a PNG, uploading it, and typing `image:<name>`, and a link to the Factbook means pasting a URL that breaks if the site moves. The preview under the textarea uses the admin console's styling, so nobody sees the page as a visitor will until after `cms publish`.\n\nGoal: turn the CMS from a Markdown publishing tool into a document-style authoring environment. Nontechnical staff can write, paste, build tables and charts, and preview the exact public result without ever seeing the underlying content format.\n\n## Solution\n\n- The **Editor**, a hand-built visual editor, replaces the Markdown textarea. It has a toolbar, cleans up pasted text, and turns a range pasted from Excel or Sheets into a table. The body is still **stored as Markdown**, so the sanitizer, `cms publish`, and existing content are unchanged (ADR-005).\n- Tables are built and edited in place.\n- A **Chart** is built from data typed or pasted into the CMS and drawn by the server as inline SVG, with its data available as a table (ADR-006, which reverses ADR-004's deferral). Uploaded **Chart images** stay and get an \"Insert image\" button.\n- Links to other Reports and Data Bites are picked from a list and stored by immutable reference, so they stay correct when slugs or the site's address change.\n- A **Site preview** shows the draft as the public page (site nav, stylesheet, date line) beside the Editor and in a new tab, with a \"Draft preview, not published\" banner.\n\nControls are functional and minimally styled. A visual design pass for the admin console comes later, in its own spec.\n\n## User Stories\n\n1. As an Analyst, I want to write a Data Bite with toolbar buttons for bold, italic, lists, headings, and quotes, so that I never have to learn Markdown.\n2. As an Analyst, I want to paste text from Word or Google Docs and keep its bold, lists, headings, and links but not its fonts or colours, so that pasted content matches the site.\n3. As an Analyst, I want to paste a range from Excel or Sheets and get a table, so that I don't retype numbers.\n4. As an Analyst, I want to edit a table in place and add or remove rows and columns, so that fixing a number takes one click.\n5. As a visitor, I want numeric table columns right-aligned, so that figures line up and compare easily.\n6. As an Analyst, I want to build a bar or line chart by typing or pasting data, and see it drawn as I go, so that a survey result gets a chart without Excel exports.\n7. As an Analyst, I want a clear message next to a cell the chart can't read, so that I know exactly what to fix.\n8. As an Analyst, I want suppressed values (`*`, `<10`) to be accepted and marked as suppressed, so that a chart respects small-cell privacy rules.\n9. As a visitor using a screen reader, I want each Chart named by its title and its data available as a table, so that I get the numbers without seeing the chart.\n10. As an Analyst, I want to link to another Report or Data Bite by picking it from a list, so that the link survives slug changes and the site moving.\n11. As a visitor, I want a link to an item that isn't published to show as plain text, not a broken link.\n12. As a Director, I want to be told which items link to an item before I delete it, so that I know which pages will lose a link.\n13. As an Analyst, I want to insert an uploaded Chart image with a button that requires a description, so that I can't forget the alt text.\n14. As an Analyst or Director, I want to see the draft exactly as the public page will look, at desktop and phone widths, so that I catch problems before publishing.\n15. As an Analyst or Director, I want a warning before I leave a page with unsaved changes, so that I don't lose work.\n16. As a Director, I want opening and saving an untouched item to leave its stored body byte-for-byte unchanged, so that the Editor never rewrites content nobody edited.\n\n## Implementation Decisions\n\n### Editor and storage (T13, ADR-005)\n\n- **No dependency.** The Editor is `contenteditable` plus a toolbar in vanilla JS with no build step (ADR-002). It supports current Chrome, Safari, and Firefox.\n- **Markdown stays the storage format.** On load, the server renders the body to Editor HTML with the existing pipeline. On save, the Editor posts its HTML, and the server sanitizes it with nh3 and converts it to Markdown with stdlib `html.parser` (a new module, testable with pytest).\n- **Toolbar:** bold, italic, bulleted list, numbered list, link, Section (H2), Subsection (H3), block quote. The title stays the only H1. There's no underline, font, colour, or alignment, because Markdown can't hold them.\n- **Base version:** the edit form carries `item_base`, a SHA-256 hash of the item's stored `title`, `slug`, and `body` as the page loaded them. The form saves all three, so all three are covered. A hash of the body alone would let a stale tab overwrite someone else's newer title or slug. On save, if the stored item's hash no longer matches (someone else saved in between), the whole save is refused with \"This item changed since you opened it. Reload to see the latest version.\" Nothing is merged, and no field is written.\n- **Untouched is byte-for-byte:** the Editor posts `body_dirty=0` until the writer's first change. With `body_dirty=0` and a matching `item_base`, the server keeps the stored body exactly and ignores the posted HTML. The client can only choose \"keep what is stored\", so trusting the flag grants nothing. Opening the Editor never rewrites the body.\n- **An edited body is saved in standard Markdown form:** any body the Editor has changed is rewritten in one standard form.\n- **Locked blocks:** a top-level block the Editor can't represent shows as a read-only block reading \"This part can't be edited here\" (with a Remove button), and its original bytes are kept even when blocks around it are edited. No current content triggers this. The mechanism:\n  - **Detection:** the stored body is parsed with markdown-it. A top-level block is *supported* only if it and everything inside it is in the Editor's set: paragraph, H2, H3, bulleted and numbered list, block quote, table, a valid `chart` fence, and inline bold, italic, line break, links allowed under T14, and `image:<name>` images. Anything else locks the whole top-level block it sits in, e.g. a code block, raw HTML, H1 or H4 and deeper, a horizontal rule, or an inline code span in a paragraph. Its exact source bytes come from the token's line map.\n  - **Before rendering Editor HTML:** each locked block is cut out of the source and replaced by an opaque token (`locked-<n>`, n being its position among the stored body's locked blocks). The remaining Markdown is rendered, and the token becomes the read-only block. The block's **raw Markdown bytes never reach the browser**: not in the Editor's HTML, not in a hidden field, not in an attribute. What the writer sees is that block's **sanitized rendered HTML** from the ordinary pipeline, displayed read-only next to its token.\n  - **On save:** each token in the posted HTML is replaced by the original fragment taken from the **stored database body** (checked by `item_base`), never from anything the client sent. A token that doesn't exist in the stored body, or appears more than once, refuses the save. A missing token means the writer removed that block, which is allowed.\n- **Paste:** only supported formatting survives. An HTML table on the clipboard (from Excel or Sheets) becomes an Editor table. A pasted or dropped picture is refused with a message pointing to \"Insert image\" (T18).\n- **Unsaved changes:** a `beforeunload` warning is shown when the Editor is dirty. There's no autosave, since that would publish half-finished text on a published Data Bite.\n- **Fallback:** the Editor takes over the existing `body` textarea. If the script fails, the textarea still works and posts Markdown as it does today.\n\n### Links (T14)\n\n- **The rule, restated:** every *site-owned* link and asset uses a relative path. Only an *explicit external link* (`<a href>`) may be absolute, and only as `https:` or `mailto:`. The Editor's link dialog refuses anything else (`http:`, `javascript:`, root-absolute `/…`, other schemes) with a message.\n- **The link pipeline enforces it for every body, however it was saved:** at render time, an `<a>` keeps its href only if the href is `https:`, `mailto:`, or a site reference (below) that resolves. Anything else renders as its link text with no `<a>`. This covers the Markdown fallback and any stored content, not only the Editor. Consequence (approved): a relative path typed by hand, e.g. `[CDS](reports/cds.html)`, renders as plain text, because it would break depending on page depth. Site links are made with the picker.\n- **Images follow the same rule:** only `image:<name>` renders an `<img>`. An absolute image URL (e.g. `![Logo](https://…)`) renders nothing (approved). A hot-linked image sits outside the draft gate that ADR-004 exists for. T14 updates `tests/test_t10_chart_images.py`'s \"other image URLs\" test to match.\n- **Stable references, not ids:** SQLite may reuse the highest deleted `INTEGER PRIMARY KEY` (noted in `app/data_bites.py` and `app/reports.py`), so the id isn't safe to link by.\n  - Each Data Bite and Report gets an immutable `ref` column: 32 lowercase hex characters from `secrets.token_hex(16)`, set at creation, never edited, never reused. {"parentUuid":"7192718d-70d9-4dd0-827c-03aeb6134a77","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"b5d8e10d-39b1-42ba-b465-8f79a0345ab4","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_014QqEHM2Mo4dKXzimtbNXz1","type":"tool_result","content":"\"\"\"SQLite access. Every table's schema lives here, so init_db() builds them all.\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport sqlite3\nfrom collections.abc import Iterator\nfrom contextlib import contextmanager\n\nfrom app import settings\n\nSCHEMA = \"\"\"\nCREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS users (\n    id            INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,\n    email         TEXT    NOT NULL UNIQUE COLLATE NOCASE,\n    name          TEXT    NOT NULL,\n    role          TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (role IN ('admin', 'editor')),\n    password_hash TEXT    NOT NULL,\n    is_active     INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,\n    created_at    TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now'))\n);\n\nCREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS data_bites (\n    id         INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,\n    title      TEXT    NOT NULL,\n    slug       TEXT    NOT NULL UNIQUE,\n    body       TEXT    NOT NULL,  -- raw Markdown; sanitized only when rendered\n    status     TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT 'draft' CHECK (status IN ('draft', 'published')),\n    author_id  INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES users (id),\n    created_at TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now')),\n    updated_at TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now')),\n    ref        TEXT    -- what a site link names it by (app.site_links); never changes\n);\n\nCREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS reports (\n    id         INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,\n    title      TEXT    NOT NULL,\n    slug       TEXT    NOT NULL UNIQUE,  -- unique among Reports only; a Data Bite may share it\n    body       TEXT    NOT NULL,  -- raw Markdown; sanitized only when rendered\n    status     TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT 'draft' CHECK (status IN ('draft', 'published')),\n    author_id  INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES users (id),\n    created_at TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now')),\n    updated_at TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now')),\n    file_name  TEXT,   -- the attached PDF's sanitized name for display; NULL if none\n    ref        TEXT    -- what a site link names it by (app.site_links); never changes\n);\n\n-- The ref of each deleted Data Bite and Report (kind: \"data-bite\" or\n-- \"report\"), so a link to one reads as deleted, and no new item reuses it.\nCREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS deleted_refs (\n    ref        TEXT PRIMARY KEY,\n    kind       TEXT NOT NULL,\n    deleted_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now'))\n);\n\"\"\"\n\n# Columns added after a table was first created: (table, column, definition).\n# CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS leaves an existing table alone, so init_db adds\n# any of these an older database is missing.\nADDED_COLUMNS = [\n    (\"reports\", \"file_name\", \"TEXT\"),\n    (\"data_bites\", \"ref\", \"TEXT\"),\n    (\"reports\", \"ref\", \"TEXT\"),\n]\n# The tables whose rows have a ref. Built after ADDED_COLUMNS, which may add\n# the column: a unique index, and a trigger that keeps a ref from changing\n# once set.\n_REF_TABLES = (\"data_bites\", \"reports\")\n_REF_RULES = \"\"\"\nCREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS {table}_ref ON {table} (ref);\nCREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS {table}_ref_fixed BEFORE UPDATE OF ref ON {table}\n    WHEN OLD.ref IS NOT NULL AND NEW.ref IS NOT OLD.ref\n    BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'a ref never changes'); END;\n\"\"\"\n\n\n@contextmanager\ndef connect() -> Iterator[sqlite3.Connection]:\n    \"\"\"Open the database named by settings (read at call time, so tests can swap\n    it). Commits on success, rolls back on error, always closes.\"\"\"\n    conn = sqlite3.connect(settings.DATABASE_PATH)\n    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row\n    conn.execute(\"PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON\")\n    try:\n        with conn:\n            yield conn\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n\n\ndef init_db() -> None:\n    # Imported here: app.site_links reads the database through this module.\n    from app import site_links\n\n    with connect() as conn:\n        conn.executescript(SCHEMA)\n        for table, column, definition in ADDED_COLUMNS:\n            existing = {row[\"name\"] for row in conn.execute(f\"PRAGMA table_info({table})\")}\n            if column not in existing:\n                conn.execute(f\"ALTER TABLE {table} ADD COLUMN {column} {definition}\")\n        for table in _REF_TABLES:\n            conn.executescript(_REF_RULES.format(table=table))\n            # Rows made before refs existed get one now.\n            for (row_id,) in conn.execute(\n                    f\"SELECT id FROM {table} WHERE ref IS NULL\").fetchall():\n                conn.execute(f\"UPDATE {table} SET ref = ? WHERE id = ?\",\n                             (site_links.new_ref(conn), row_id))\n\"\"\"`cms publish`: write the public site into site/ as plain HTML.\n\nThe pages and files come from app.public_site, the same ones the app serves,\nat the same paths, so the export is the live public site rather than a second\nrendering of it. That module reads only published content and links only\nrelatively, which gives the two rules the rubric checks here:\n\n  1. Only PUBLISHED content is written here. A draft that reaches site/ is a bug.\n  2. Every href and src is RELATIVE (\"style.css\", \"reports/x.html\"), never\n     root-absolute (\"/style.css\"), because Pages serves this from a subfolder.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport shutil\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom app import public_site, settings\n\n\ndef render_site(out: Path | None = None) -> Path:\n    \"\"\"Regenerate `out` (site/ by default) from scratch, so a page taken down\n    since the last publish is gone from it too.\"\"\"\n    out = out or settings.SITE\n    if out.exists():\n        shutil.rmtree(out)\n    out.mkdir(parents=True)\n    # UTF-8, as the app serves them, whatever this machine's locale.\n    (out / \"style.css\").write_text(public_site.CSS, encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    for page in public_site.pages():\n        _target(out, page.path).write_text(page.render(), encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    for path, stored in public_site.files().items():\n        shutil.copyfile(stored, _target(out, path))\n    return out\n\n\ndef _target(out: Path, path: str) -> Path:\n    \"\"\"Where `path` in the site goes under `out`, its folder made.\"\"\"\n    target = out / path\n    target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    return target\n        preview's own copy of the site, an admin path ending in \"/\". Its links\n        stay relative, as in the export, and a <base> puts the page at its\n        path under `at`, where they reach the preview's stylesheet and files.\n        It shows the \"Draft preview, not published\" banner.\"\"\"\n        return self._render(preview_base=f\"{at}{self.path}\")\n\n    def _render(self, *, preview_base: str | None) -> str:\n        root = \"../\" * self.path.count(\"/\")\n\n        def image_src(name: str) -> str | None:\n            path = self.images.get(name)\n            return None if path is None else f\"{root}{path}\"\n\n        links = published_links() if self.links is None else self.links\n\n        def link_href(reference: str) -> str | None:\n            path = links.get(reference)\n            return None if path is None else f\"{root}{path}\"\n\n        nav_reports = reports.list_published() if self.nav_reports is None else self.nav_reports\n        return templates.env.get_template(self.template).render(\n            image_src=image_src, link_href=link_href,\n            title=settings.SITE_TITLE, root=root, css_path=f\"{root}style.css\",\n            home_path=f\"{root}index.html\", nav_reports=nav_reports,\n            data_bite_path=data_bite_path, report_path=report_path,\n            report_file_path=report_file_path, preview_base=preview_base, **self.context)\n\n\ndef published_links() -> dict[str, str]:\n    \"\"\"Where a site link to each published item leads, {site reference: path\n    in the site}. A draft, deleted, or unknown one is not here, so a link to\n    it is its text.\"\"\"\n    return {**{site_links.reference(\"data-bite\", bite[\"ref\"]): data_bite_path(bite[\"slug\"])\n               for bite in data_bites.list_published()},\n            **{site_links.reference(\"report\", found[\"ref\"]): report_path(found[\"slug\"])\n               for found in reports.list_published()}}\n\n\ndef _linked_as_published(page: Page, kind: str, item: Mapping) -> Page:\n    \"\"\"A Site preview's page, whose item's own site links resolve as if it\n    were published; a new item has no ref yet.\"\"\"\n    links = published_links()\n    if item.get(\"ref\"):\n        links[site_links.reference(kind, item[\"ref\"])] = page.path\n    return replace(page, links=links)\n\n\ndef home() -> Page:\n    return Page(\"index.html\", \"public/home.html\",\n                {\"data_bites\": data_bites.list_published()[:RECENT_DATA_BITES]})\n\n\ndef data_bite_list() -> Page:\n    return Page(\"data-bites/index.html\", \"public/data_bites.html\",\n                {\"page_title\": \"Data Bites\", \"data_bites\": data_bites.list_published()})\n\n\ndef data_bite(slug: str) -> Page | None:\n    \"\"\"A published Data Bite's page; None for a draft or no such Data Bite.\"\"\"\n    bite = data_bites.get_published(slug)\n    return None if bite is None else _data_bite_page(bite)\n\n\ndef _data_bite_page(bite: Mapping) -> Page:\n    return Page(data_bite_path(bite[\"slug\"]), \"public/data_bite.html\",\n                {\"page_title\": bite[\"title\"], \"bite\": bite},\n                images={name: data_bite_image_path(bite[\"slug\"], name)\n                        for name in _stored_images(data_bites, bite)})\n\n\ndef _stored_images(module: ModuleType, item: Mapping) -> dict[str, Path]:\n    \"\"\"A Data Bite's or Report's chart images (`module` is its type's),\n    {name: where it is stored}; none for one not yet saved.\"\"\"\n    return {} if item[\"id\"] is None else module.images(item[\"id\"])\n\n\ndef data_bite_files(bite: Mapping) -> dict[str, Path]:\n    \"\"\"The files a Data Bite's page links to, its chart images, as {path in\n    the site: where it is stored}.\"\"\"\n    return {data_bite_image_path(bite[\"slug\"], name): path\n            for name, path in _stored_images(data_bites, bite).items()}\n\n\ndef data_bite_image(slug: str, name: str) -> Path | None:\n    \"\"\"Where a published Data Bite's chart image, at\n    data_bite_image_path(slug, name) in the site, is stored. None for a\n    draft, no such image, or no such Data Bite.\"\"\"\n    bite = data_bites.get_published(slug)\n    return None if bite is None else data_bites.images(bite[\"id\"]).get(name)\n\n\ndef report_list() -> Page:\n    return Page(\"reports/index.html\", \"public/reports.html\",\n                {\"page_title\": \"Reports\", \"reports\": reports.list_published()})\n\n\ndef _stored_file(report: Mapping) -> Path | None:\n    \"\"\"Where the Report's file is stored, if it has one and it is there.\"\"\"\n    if report[\"file_name\"] is None:\n        return None\n    stored = reports.file_path(report[\"id\"])\n    return stored if stored.is_file() else None\n\n\ndef report(slug: str) -> Page | None:\n    \"\"\"A published Report's page, linking its file only if that can be\n    downloaded; None for a draft or no such Report.\"\"\"\n    found = reports.get_published(slug)\n    return None if found is None else _report_page(found)\n\n\ndef _report_page(found: Mapping) -> Page:\n    return Page(report_path(found[\"slug\"]), \"public/report.html\",\n                {\"page_title\": found[\"title\"], \"report\": found,\n                 \"has_file\": _stored_file(found) is not None},\n                images={name: report_image_path(found[\"slug\"], name)\n                        for name in _stored_images(reports, found)})\n\n\ndef report_image_files(found: Mapping) -> dict[str, Path]:\n    \"\"\"A Report's chart images, as {path in the site: where it is stored}.\"\"\"\n    return {report_image_path(found[\"slug\"], name): path\n            for name, path in _stored_images(reports, found).items()}\n\n\ndef report_pdf_file(found: Mapping) -> dict[str, Path]:\n    \"\"\"A Report's file, if its page links to it (it can be downloaded), as\n    {path in the site: where it is stored}; empty if not.\"\"\"\n    stored = _stored_file(found)\n    return {report_file_path(found[\"slug\"]): stored} if stored else {}\n\n\ndef report_files(found: Mapping) -> dict[str, Path]:\n    \"\"\"Every file a Report's page links to, as {path in the site: where it is\n    stored}.\"\"\"\n    return {**report_image_files(found), **report_pdf_file(found)}\n\n\ndef report_file(slug: str) -> tuple[Path, str] | None:\n    \"\"\"A published Report's attached file, at report_file_path(slug) in the\n    site, as (where it is stored, its display name). None for a draft, a\n    Report with no file, or no such Report.\"\"\"\n    found = reports.get_published(slug)\n    stored = found and _stored_file(found)\n    return (stored, found[\"file_name\"]) if stored else None\n\n\ndef report_image(slug: str, name: str) -> Path | None:\n    \"\"\"Where a published Report's chart image, at report_image_path(slug,\n    name) in the site, is stored. None for a draft, no such image, or no such\n    Report.\"\"\"\n    found = reports.get_published(slug)\n    return None if found is None else reports.images(found[\"id\"]).get(name)\n\n\ndef pages() -> list[Page]:\n    \"\"\"Every page of the site: what `cms publish` writes.\"\"\"\n    return [home(), data_bite_list(), report_list(),\n            *map(_data_bite_page, data_bites.list_published()),\n            *map(_report_page, reports.list_published())]\n\n\ndef files() -> dict[str, Path]:\n    \"\"\"Every file the site's pages link to besides the stylesheet, as\n    {path in the site: where it is stored}: the published Data Bites' and\n    Reports' chart images, and the published Reports' files.\"\"\"\n    found: dict[str, Path] = {}\n    for bite in data_bites.list_published():\n        found.update(data_bite_files(bite))\n    for report in reports.list_published():\n        found.update(report_files(report))\n    return found\n\n\n# Site previews: one item's page, as if it were published, with unsaved edits.\n\ndef _as_if_published(form: Mapping[str, str], saved: sqlite3.Row | None) -> dict:\n    \"\"\"The item a Site preview shows: `saved` (None for a new item, dated now)\n    with `form`'s unsaved title and body, published. Every table's schema lives here, so init_db() builds them all.\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport sqlite3\nfrom collections.abc import Iterator\nfrom contextlib import contextmanager\n\nfrom app import settings\n\nSCHEMA = \"\"\"\nCREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS users (\n    id            INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,\n    email         TEXT    NOT NULL UNIQUE COLLATE NOCASE,\n    name          TEXT    NOT NULL,\n    role          TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (role IN ('admin', 'editor')),\n    password_hash TEXT    NOT NULL,\n    is_active     INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,\n    created_at    TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now'))\n);\n\nCREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS data_bites (\n    id         INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,\n    title      TEXT    NOT NULL,\n    slug       TEXT    NOT NULL UNIQUE,\n    body       TEXT    NOT NULL,  -- raw Markdown; sanitized only when rendered\n    status     TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT 'draft' CHECK (status IN ('draft', 'published')),\n    author_id  INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES users (id),\n    created_at TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now')),\n    updated_at TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now')),\n    ref        TEXT    -- what a site link names it by (app.site_links); never changes\n);\n\nCREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS reports (\n    id         INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,\n    title      TEXT    NOT NULL,\n    slug       TEXT    NOT NULL UNIQUE,  -- unique among Reports only; Built after ADDED_COLUMNS, which may add\n# the column: a unique index, and a trigger that keeps a ref from changing\n# once set.\n_REF_TABLES = (\"data_bites\", \"reports\")\n_REF_RULES = \"\"\"\nCREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS {table}_ref ON {table} (ref);\nCREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS {table}_ref_fixed BEFORE UPDATE OF ref ON {table}\n    WHEN OLD.ref IS NOT NULL AND NEW.ref IS NOT OLD.ref\n    BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'a ref never changes'); END;\n\"\"\"\n\n\n@contextmanager\ndef connect() -> Iterator[sqlite3.Connection]:\n    \"\"\"Open the database named by settings (read at call time, so tests can swap\n    it). Commits on success, rolls back on error, always closes.\"\"\"\n    conn = sqlite3.connect(settings.DATABASE_PATH)\n    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row\n    conn.execute(\"PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON\")\n    try:\n        with conn:\n            yield conn\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n\n\ndef init_db() -> None:\n    # Imported here: app.site_links reads the database through this module.\n    from app import site_links\n\n    with connect() as conn:\n        conn.executescript(SCHEMA)\n        for table, column, definition in ADDED_COLUMNS:\n            existing = {row[\"name\"] for row in conn.execute(f\"PRAGMA table_info({table})\")}\n            if column not in existing:\n                conn.execute(f\"ALTER TABLE {table} ADD COLUMN {column} {definition}\")\n        for table in _REF_TABLES:\n            conn.executescript(_REF_RULES.format(table=table))\n            # Rows made before refs existed get one now.\n            for (row_id,) in conn.execute(\n                    f\"SELECT id FROM {table} WHERE ref IS NULL\").fetchall():\n                conn.execute(f\"UPDATE {table} SET ref = ? WHERE id = ?\",\n                             (site_links.new_ref(conn), row_id))\n\"\"\"`cms publish`: write the public site into site/ as plain HTML.\n\nThe pages and files come from app.public_site, the same ones the app serves,\nat the same paths, so the export is the live public site rather than a second\nrendering of it. That module reads only published content and links only\nrelatively, which gives the two rules the rubric checks here:\n\n  1. Only PUBLISHED content is written here. Every href and src is RELATIVE (\"style.css\", \"reports/x.html\"), never\n     root-absolute (\"/style.css\"), because Pages serves this from a subfolder.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport shutil\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom app import public_site, settings\n\n\ndef render_site(out: Path | None = None) -> Path:\n    \"\"\"Regenerate `out` (site/ by default) from scratch, so a page taken down\n    since the last publish is gone from it too.\"\"\"\n    out = out or settings.SITE\n    if out.exists():\n        shutil.rmtree(out)\n    out.mkdir(parents=True)\n    # UTF-8, as the app serves them, whatever this machine's locale.\n    (out / \"style.css\").write_text(public_site.CSS, encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    for page in public_site.pages():\n        _target(out, page.path).write_text(page.render(), encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    for path, stored in public_site.files().items():\n        shutil.copyfile(stored, _target(out, path))\n    return out\n\n\ndef _target(out: Path, path: str) -> Path:\n    \"\"\"Where `path` in the site goes under `out`, its folder made.\"\"\"\n    target = out / path\n    target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    return target\n        preview's own copy of the site, an admin path ending in \"/\". {"parentUuid":"92d52039-d0f1-4643-92b4-d211bbd39102","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011CfbtpgtMZkWjvUsJHepzm","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01SMYVcQNtvbHc1zmhadNYCg","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-davelleat-code-iphs400-mp2-cms/eae09489-d0ef-4a1c-b220-1610b02a6314/scratchpad/spec-22.md","content":"## Problem Statement\n\nThe public site works, but it has no design. It is about 20 lines of CSS in `app/public_site.py`: one 42rem column, the system font, browser-blue links, and a homepage that is just a list of titles. A visitor can't tell what the office publishes, which numbers matter, or how recent they are. Compared with what a WordPress theme gives an office on day one, it looks unfinished. The office also has no way to change its homepage, no summary to show under a title in a list or in a shared link, and no search.\n\nGoal: a public site that looks considered and distinctive, reads well on a phone, and is clearly a college's official data office. Plus the three things a WordPress site gets without effort: an editable homepage, summaries, and search.\n\n## Solution\n\nA visual design, **\"set like a dataset\"**, approved from a mockup in session 22 (screenshots in the closing comment of T19):\n\n- **Type:** Atkinson Hyperlegible Next for text and Atkinson Hyperlegible Mono for figures and labels. The Braille Institute designed them so 0/O and 1/l/I can't be confused, which suits a site of numbers. Self-hosted `.woff2`, OFL.\n- **Colour:** Kenyon purple `#4B2E84` and Kenyon bright purple `#8F80FF` (Kenyon brand guide), a deep purple field `#231443` with a faint plotting grid behind the header, and a single citron accent `#D6F550` used **only** on the purple field. Paper `#FBFAFD`. A full dark mode.\n- **Structure:** numbered navigation (`01 Factbook`), numbered home sections, ISO dates (`2026-09-29`), Reports listed in a real table, and an item's title, summary, and facts set on the purple field above its body.\n- **Charts:** the existing drawn Charts (T16), recoloured. The last series, the newest, is Kenyon purple and earlier series are bright purple. A single series is Kenyon purple.\n\nAnd three features:\n\n- A **Summary** on every Data Bite and Report, shown under its title, in lists, and in link previews.\n- **Homepage settings** the Director edits: the headline, the intro, and up to four **Key figures**. The homepage also features the latest Data Bite with its first Chart.\n- **Site search**, entirely static: `cms publish` writes an index of published titles and summaries, and a small script searches it.\n\nThe admin console keeps today's look. Its redesign is a later spec.\n\n## User Stories\n\n1. As a visitor, I want the homepage to show the college's key figures first, so that I get the most-asked numbers without clicking.\n2. As a visitor, I want to see the latest Data Bite and its chart on the homepage, so that I know what's new and current.\n3. As a visitor, I want Reports listed with what each covers, when it was updated, and whether it's a PDF, so that I can pick the right one at a glance.\n4. As a visitor, I want every Data Bite and Report to have a one- or two-sentence summary under its title and in lists, so that I can tell items apart without opening them.\n5. As a visitor sharing a link, I want the preview in Slack, email, or social media to show the item's title and summary, so that the link is self-explanatory.\n6. As a visitor, I want to search Reports and Data Bites by title and summary, so that I can find \"retention\" without browsing.\n7. As a visitor on a phone, I want every page readable at 390 px with nothing scrolling sideways except a wide table or the nav, so that the site works where most people read it.\n8. As a visitor with low vision or using a keyboard, I want legible type, AA contrast, a skip link, and a visible focus ring, so that I can use the site.\n9. As a visitor using dark mode, I want the site to follow it, so that it isn't a white flash at night.\n10. As a visitor who follows a broken link, I want a site-styled \"page not found\" with a way home, not GitHub's default.\n11. As a visitor printing a Report, I want a clean black-on-white printout without the nav or the purple header.\n12. As the Director, I want to change the homepage headline, intro, and key figures in the console, so that the homepage changes with the census, not with a code change.\n13. As an Analyst or Director, I want to write a summary when I edit an item, with a length limit shown as I type, so that summaries stay short.\n14. As an Analyst or Director, I want the Site preview to show the new design, summary included, so that the preview is still the page as published.\n\n## Implementation Decisions\n\n### Shared (ADR-007)\n\n- **No new dependency.** The fonts are static files in `static/fonts/` with their OFL licence. `cms publish` copies them to `site/fonts/`, and the app serves them at `fonts/…`. No CDN: the site must work from a GitHub Pages subfolder with relative paths only (ADR-001).\n- **The stylesheet moves out of Python** into `static/site.css`, served at `style.css` and written there by `cms publish`, as now. `app.public_site.CSS` goes, and every reader of it (the publish step, the stylesheet route, the preview's copy of the site) reads the file.\n- **The admin console gets its own stylesheet**, `static/admin.css`: today's base rules plus every `.admin-*` rule, and the `.content-body`/`.chart-*` rules the Editor and Chart builder need. `base.html` stays the admin layout, and `public/layout.html` becomes a standalone public layout. A public rule must never reach an admin page, and an admin rule must never reach the public site.\n- Class names keep the repo's prefix rule (`.nav-site`, `.figures-home`, `.table-reports`); no bare `.title` or `.status`.\n- **Dates:** ISO `YYYY-MM-DD` everywhere on the public site, in Atkinson Mono.\n\n### T19: Look and feel\n\n- The layout, header, nav, footer, and type described above, on every public page: home, the Data Bites list, the Reports list, a Data Bite, a Report, and a Site preview (banner restyled to match).\n- **Nav:** each published Report in title order, then Data Bites, each numbered `01`, `02`, … in mono. The current page is marked with `aria-current=\"page\"` and a citron underline. On a phone the nav scrolls sideways with a fade at the edge, and never wraps under the header.\n- **Item pages:** breadcrumb, title, and a facts row (Published, Type, a Report's PDF download) on the purple field. The body sits below at a 44rem measure.\n- **Tables (T09) and Charts (T16):** restyled by class only. Hairline rules, mono figures in right-aligned columns, and the series colours above. The Chart text keeps the size its layout assumes (`FONT` in `app/chart_drawing.py`), and a figure is capped at the 40rem width it is drawn for, so its labels don't scale up in a wider column.\n- **Homepage in T19:** the new layout with the content there is today: the latest Data Bites and the Reports. The key figures, headline, and featured Chart wait for T20.\n- **Search box in the header:** not shown until T20.\n- **Accessibility:** skip link, `:focus-visible` ring, `prefers-reduced-motion` respected, and text contrast ≥ 4.5:1 (≥ 3:1 for large text and chart marks) in both themes, checked and recorded.\n- **Print:** a print stylesheet with black on white, no header field, nav, or search, and link URLs not appended (they're relative).\n- **404:** `cms publish` writes `404.html` at the site root (GitHub Pages serves it for any missing path). It uses the site layout and links home. Because it can be served at any depth, its links and assets use the site's base path from a `<base>` set from `settings.SITE_URL_PATH`, or, if that is unset, absolute-free links to `index.html` that work at the root. The exact mechanism is settled in T19, keeping the relative-links rule.\n\n### T20: Homepage, summaries, and search\n\n- **Summary:** a `summary TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT ''` column on `data_bites` and `reports` (via `ADDED_COLUMNS`). Plain text, trimmed, at most 200 characters, refused over that with a message by the field. No Markdown, and it's escaped by Jinja like the title. It's on both edit forms under the title, with a live character count. It's optional: an item without one shows nothing in its place.\n- **Where a Summary shows:** under the title on the item page, in the Data Bites list, in the Reports table's \"What it covers\", on the homepage's latest Data Bite, and in `<meta name=\"description\">`, `og:title`, `og:description`, and `og:type`. `og:url` and `og:image` are left out, because they need absolute URLs.\n- **Homepage settings:** a new `homepage` table holding one row: `headline`, `headline_accent` (the part shown in bright purple), `intro`, and up to four key figures, each with a `value`, a `label`, and a `note` (e.g. \"1,805\" / \"Students enrolled\" / \"Fall 2026 census\"). All of it is plain text with length limits, escaped. It's edited on a Director-only page, `/admin/homepage`, with a CSRF token, and an Analyst gets 403. It has no draft state: it's settings, not content, so it appears on the next `cms publish` like a nav change does. The fixed Confirmation is \"Homepage saved.\" Defaults are seeded so a fresh site has a sensible homepage.\n- **Featured Data Bite:** the newest published Data Bite, with its Summary and its **first Chart** if its body has one, drawn by the existing chart pipeline. Without a Chart, it shows only its title, Summary, and link.\n- **Reports table:** Report, Summary, Updated (`updated_at` date), and Format (`PDF` if its file can be downloaded, otherwise `WEB`). It stacks into rows on a phone.\n- **Search:**\n  - `cms publish` writes `search-index.json`: published items only, with `kind`, `title`, `summary`, `date`, and a site-relative `path`. Nothing from a draft, not even a title, is in it.\n  - `search.html` plus `static/search.js` (vanilla, no build step, ADR-002) does a case-insensitive, accent-insensitive match on title and summary, ranking title matches first.\n  - The header form is a plain `GET` to `search.html?q=`.\n  - Without JavaScript, `search.html` lists every published item, so the form still leads somewhere useful.\n  - The app serves both files too, so search works in local preview as well.\n- **Glossary:** CONTEXT.md gains **Summary**, **Homepage settings**, **Key figure**, and **Site search**.\n\n## Testing Decisions\n\n- Existing tests keep passing. Any test that asserts on today's markup or `public_site.CSS` is updated to the new markup in the same commit, with the reason given.\n- New tests:\n  - The stylesheet and fonts are served and exported, and `site/` contains no root-absolute `href` or `src` (the existing crawler).\n  - No public page links `admin.css`, and no admin page links `site.css`.\n  - The Summary's limit and escaping.\n  - Homepage settings are Director-only and need CSRF.\n  - The search index holds published items only: a draft's title must not appear in it.\n  - The featured Data Bite shows its first Chart, and nothing when it has none.\n  - `404.html` exists in the export.\n- **Browser check** in each closing comment, at 390, 768, and 1440 px (the iframe method in the session notes) in light and dark, with screenshots. Plus a check that the fonts actually loaded (`document.fonts`), not just that they are named in the CSS.\n\n## Out of Scope\n\n- The admin console's redesign (a later spec).\n- Full-text search of bodies, and a search server.\n- `og:image`, social cards, and analytics.\n- Report categories in the nav.\n- Theme switching or a theme picker in the console.\n\n## Further Notes\n\n- Mockup and fonts from session 22 are in that session's scratchpad. The approved mockup's CSS is the starting point for `static/site.css`.\n- Kenyon brand colours: [Kenyon brand guide](https://www.kenyon.edu/files/resources/brand-guides-brand-08-30-23.pdf).\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":6630,"cache_read_input_tokens":170743,"output_tokens":6058,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":1835},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":6630,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"not_available","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":6058,"cache_read_input_tokens":170743,"cache_creation_input_tokens":6630,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":6630},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"wireToolInputs":{"toolu_01SMYVcQNtvbHc1zmhadNYCg":{"file_path":"/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-davelleat-code-iphs400-mp2-cms/eae09489-d0ef-4a1c-b220-1610b02a6314/scratchpad/spec-22.md","content":"## Problem Statement\n\nThe public site works, but it has no design. A public rule must never reach an admin page, and an admin rule must never reach the public site.\n- Class names keep the repo's prefix rule (`.nav-site`, `.figures-home`, `.table-reports`); no bare `.title` or `.status`.\n- **Dates:** ISO `YYYY-MM-DD` everywhere on the public site, in Atkinson Mono.\n\n### T19: Look and feel\n\n- The layout, header, nav, footer, and type described above, on every public page: home, the Data Bites list, the Reports list, a Data Bite, a Report, and a Site preview (banner restyled to match).\n- **Nav:** each published Report in title order, then Data Bites, each numbered `01`, `02`, … in mono. The current page is marked with `aria-current=\"page\"` and a citron underline. On a phone the nav scrolls sideways with a fade at the edge, and never wraps under the header.\n- **Item pages:** breadcrumb, title, and a facts row (Published, Type, a Report's PDF download) on the purple field. The body sits below at a 44rem measure.\n- **Tables (T09) and Charts (T16):** restyled by class only. Hairline rules, mono figures in right-aligned columns, and the series colours above. The Chart text keeps the size its layout assumes (`FONT` in `app/chart_drawing.py`), and a figure is capped at the 40rem width it is drawn for, so its labels don't scale up in a wider column.\n- **Homepage in T19:** the new layout with the content there is today: the latest Data Bites and the Reports. The key figures, headline, and featured Chart wait for T20.\n- **Search box in the header:** not shown until T20.\n- **Accessibility:** skip link, `:focus-visible` ring, `prefers-reduced-motion` respected, and text contrast ≥ 4.5:1 (≥ 3:1 for large text and chart marks) in both themes, checked and recorded.\n- **Print:** a print stylesheet with black on white, no header field, nav, or search, and link URLs not appended (they're relative).\n- **404:** `cms publish` writes `404.html` at the site root (GitHub Pages serves it for any missing path). It uses the site layout and links home. Because it can be served at any depth, its links and assets use the site's base path from a `<base>` set from `settings.SITE_URL_PATH`, or, if that is unset, absolute-free links to `index.html` that work at the root. The exact mechanism is settled in T19, keeping the relative-links rule.\n\n### T20: Homepage, summaries, and search\n\n- **Summary:** a `summary TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT ''` column on `data_bites` and `reports` (via `ADDED_COLUMNS`). Plain text, trimmed, at most 200 characters, refused over that with a message by the field. No Markdown, and it's escaped by Jinja like the title. It's on both edit forms under the title, with a live character count. It's optional: an item without one shows nothing in its place.\n- **Where a Summary shows:** under the title on the item page, in the Data Bites list, in the Reports table's \"What it covers\", on the homepage's latest Data Bite, and in `<meta name=\"description\">`, `og:title`, `og:description`, and `og:type`. `og:url` and `og:image` are left out, because they need absolute URLs.\n- **Homepage settings:** a new `homepage` table holding one row: `headline`, `headline_accent` (the part shown in bright purple), `intro`, and up to four key figures, each with a `value`, a `label`, and a `note` (e.g. \"1,805\" / \"Students enrolled\" / \"Fall 2026 census\"). All of it is plain text with length limits, escaped. It's edited on a Director-only page, `/admin/homepage`, with a CSRF token, and an Analyst gets 403. It has no draft state: it's settings, not content, so it appears on the next `cms publish` like a nav change does. The fixed Confirmation is \"Homepage saved.\" Defaults are seeded so a fresh site has a sensible homepage.\n- **Featured Data Bite:** the newest published Data Bite, with its Summary and its **first Chart** if its body has one, drawn by the existing chart pipeline. Without a Chart, it shows only its title, Summary, and link.\n- **Reports table:** Report, Summary, Updated (`updated_at` date), and Format (`PDF` if its file can be downloaded, otherwise `WEB`). It stacks into rows on a phone.\n- **Search:**\n  - `cms publish` writes `search-index.json`: published items only, with `kind`, `title`, `summary`, `date`, and a site-relative `path`. Nothing from a draft, not even a title, is in it.\n  - `search.html` plus `static/search.js` (vanilla, no build step, ADR-002) does a case-insensitive, accent-insensitive match on title and summary, ranking title matches first.\n  - The header form is a plain `GET` to `search.html?q=`.\n  - Without JavaScript, `search.html` lists every published item, so the form still leads somewhere useful.\n  - The app serves both files too, so search works in local preview as well.\n- **Glossary:** CONTEXT.md gains **Summary**, **Homepage settings**, **Key figure**, and **Site search**.\n\n## Testing Decisions\n\n- Existing tests keep passing. Any test that asserts on today's markup or `public_site.CSS` is updated to the new markup in the same commit, with the reason given.\n- New tests:\n  - The stylesheet and fonts are served and exported, and `site/` contains no root-absolute `href` or `src` (the existing crawler).\n  - No public page links `admin.css`, and no admin page links `site.css`.\n  - The Summary's limit and escaping.\n  - Homepage settings are Director-only and need CSRF.\n  - The search index holds published items only: a draft's title must not appear in it.\n  - The featured Data Bite shows its first Chart, and nothing when it has none.\n  - `404.html` exists in the export.\n- **Browser check** in each closing comment, at 390, 768, and 1440 px (the iframe method in the session notes) in light and dark, with screenshots. Plus a check that the fonts actually loaded (`document.fonts`), not just that they are named in the CSS.\n\n## Out of Scope\n\n- The admin console's redesign (a later spec).\n- Full-text search of bodies, and a search server.\n- `og:image`, social cards, and analytics.\n- Report categories in the nav.\n- Theme switching or a theme picker in the console.\n\n## Further Notes\n\n- Mockup and fonts from session 22 are in that session's scratchpad. It is about 20 lines of CSS in `app/public_site.py`: one 42rem column, the system font, browser-blue links, and a homepage that is just a list of titles. A visitor can't tell what the office publishes, which numbers matter, or how recent they are. Compared with what a WordPress theme gives an office on day one, it looks unfinished. The office also has no way to change its homepage, no summary to show under a title in a list or in a shared link, and no search.\n\nGoal: a public site that looks considered and distinctive, reads well on a phone, and is clearly a college's official data office. Plus the three things a WordPress site gets without effort: an editable homepage, summaries, and search.\n\n## Solution\n\nA visual design, **\"set like a dataset\"**, approved from a mockup in session 22 (screenshots in the closing comment of T19):\n\n- **Type:** Atkinson Hyperlegible Next for text and Atkinson Hyperlegible Mono for figures and labels. The Braille Institute designed them so 0/O and 1/l/I can't be confused, which suits a site of numbers. Self-hosted `.woff2`, OFL.\n- **Colour:** Kenyon purple `#4B2E84` and Kenyon bright purple `#8F80FF` (Kenyon brand guide), a deep purple field `#231443` with a faint plotting grid behind the header, and a single citron accent `#D6F550` used **only** on the purple field. Paper `#FBFAFD`. A full dark mode.\n- **Structure:** numbered navigation (`01 Factbook`), numbered home sections, ISO dates (`2026-09-29`), Reports listed in a real table, and an item's title, summary, and facts set on the purple field above its body.\n- **Charts:** the existing drawn Charts (T16), recoloured. The last series, the newest, is Kenyon purple and earlier series are bright purple. A single series is Kenyon purple.\n\nAnd three features:\n\n- A **Summary** on every Data Bite and Report, shown under its title, in lists, and in link previews.\n- **Homepage settings** the Director edits: the headline, the intro, and up to four **Key figures**. The homepage also features the latest Data Bite with its first Chart.\n- **Site search**, entirely static: `cms publish` writes an index of published titles and summaries, and a small script searches it.\n\nThe admin console keeps today's look. Its redesign is a later spec.\n\n## User Stories\n\n1. As a visitor, I want the homepage to show the college's key figures first, so that I get the most-asked numbers without clicking.\n2. As a visitor, I want to see the latest Data Bite and its chart on the homepage, so that I know what's new and current.\n3. As a visitor, I want Reports listed with what each covers, when it was updated, and whether it's a PDF, so that I can pick the right one at a glance.\n4. As a visitor, I want every Data Bite and Report to have a one- or two-sentence summary under its title and in lists, so that I can tell items apart without opening them.\n5. As a visitor sharing a link, I want the preview in Slack, email, or social media to show the item's title and summary, so that the link is self-explanatory.\n6. As a visitor, I want to search Reports and Data Bites by title and summary, so that I can find \"retention\" without browsing.\n7. As a visitor on a phone, I want every page readable at 390 px with nothing scrolling sideways except a wide table or the nav, so that the site works where most people read it.\n8. As a visitor with low vision or using a keyboard, I want legible type, AA contrast, a skip link, and a visible focus ring, so that I can use the site.\n9. As a visitor using dark mode, I want the site to follow it, so that it isn't a white flash at night.\n10. As a visitor printing a Report, I want a clean black-on-white printout without the nav or the purple header.\n12. As the Director, I want to change the homepage headline, intro, and key figures in the console, so that the homepage changes with the census, not with a code change.\n13. As an Analyst or Director, I want to write a summary when I edit an item, with a length limit shown as I type, so that summaries stay short.\n14. {"parentUuid":"98e6e39a-e3be-4bba-a9f0-f7d67a9550b6","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011Cfbtvcy8Hzh9fYtWzofAr","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_017viVctRUsz9QTZ9pexn8hv","name":"Bash","input":{"command":"cd /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-davelleat-code-iphs400-mp2-cms/eae09489-d0ef-4a1c-b220-1610b02a6314/scratchpad && cat > t19.md <<'EOF'\n## Parent\n\nPart of #SPEC\n\n## What to build\n\nThe public site's new look, \"set like a dataset\", on every public page, from the approved session-22 mockup:\n\n- Atkinson Hyperlegible Next and Mono, self-hosted.\n- Kenyon purple fields with a plotting grid, and a citron accent used only on purple.\n- Numbered nav and sections, ISO dates, and restyled tables and Charts.\n- A full dark mode, a print stylesheet, and a `404.html`.\n\nThe stylesheet moves to `static/site.css`, and the admin console moves to its own `static/admin.css` with today's look unchanged (ADR-007). No new data and no new admin pages: the homepage uses what exists today.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] ADR-007 records the self-hosted fonts (OFL licence committed beside them), `static/site.css` replacing `app.public_site.CSS`, the separate `admin.css`, and the 404 page's `<base>`\n- [ ] `cms publish` writes `style.css`, `fonts/*.woff2`, and `404.html`. The app serves the stylesheet and fonts at the same relative paths\n- [ ] Every public page uses the new layout: home, the Data Bites list, the Reports list, a Data Bite, a Report, and a Site preview (banner restyled)\n- [ ] Nav: published Reports in title order, then Data Bites, numbered `01…`. The current page has `aria-current=\"page\"`. On a phone the nav scrolls sideways with an edge fade and never wraps\n- [ ] Item pages: breadcrumb, title, and the facts row (Published date, Type, and a Report's PDF download) on the purple field, with the body at a 44rem measure\n- [ ] Tables and Charts restyled by class only. Numeric columns use mono figures. Chart series: the last is Kenyon purple and the earlier ones bright purple, with a single series in Kenyon purple. A figure is capped at 40rem\n- [ ] Dates on the public site are ISO `YYYY-MM-DD`\n- [ ] Dark mode via `prefers-color-scheme`\n- [ ] Text contrast ≥ 4.5:1 (large text and chart marks ≥ 3:1) in both themes, with the pairs and ratios listed in the closing comment\n- [ ] Skip link, `:focus-visible` ring, `prefers-reduced-motion`, and a print stylesheet\n- [ ] No public page references `admin.css`, and no admin page references `site.css`. The admin console, Editor, Chart builder, and image panel look as they do today\n- [ ] The crawler passes: no root-absolute `href`/`src`, and the only `<base>` is the one in `404.html`\n- [ ] Tests updated where they asserted on old markup or `public_site.CSS` (each noted in the commit), plus the new tests listed in the spec. The whole suite passes\n- [ ] Browser check in the closing comment, with screenshots:\n  - Every page type at 390, 768, and 1440 px, in light and dark\n  - `document.fonts` shows both families loaded\n  - No horizontal page scroll at 390 px\n\n## Blocked by\n\nNone\nEOF\ncat > t20.md <<'EOF'\n## Parent\n\nPart of #SPEC\n\n## What to build\n\nThe three features that complete the homepage:\n\n- A **Summary** on every Data Bite and Report, with link-preview metadata.\n- **Homepage settings** the Director edits: headline, accent, intro, and up to four **Key figures**. {"parentUuid":"739b39cc-8715-44a5-9f28-b2f6447cadfe","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011CfbtzzVJHbeLn9eW6uoKs","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_011ftp1NjdcKybGJ85FZwZ1E","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/Users/davelleat/.claude/projects/-Users-davelleat-code-iphs400-mp2-cms/memory/design-taste.md","content":"---\nname: design-taste\ndescription: User rejects default/\"AI-ey\" visual design; what was rejected and what was approved for the public site\nmetadata:\n  type: feedback\n---\n\nThe user rejected two mockups before approving one (session 22, 2026-10-01, spec #22):\n- Rejected as \"juvenile and AI-ey\": Inter, purple gradient hero, rounded cards with shadows and coloured top borders, pill nav, uppercase eyebrows everywhere.\n- Rejected as \"everyone uses this\": the newspaper look, meaning a Newsreader-style serif, italic standfirsts, and a masthead nameplate.\n- Approved, \"set like a dataset\": Atkinson Hyperlegible Next and Mono, solid Kenyon-purple fields with a faint plotting grid, one citron accent only on purple, numbered nav and sections, ISO dates, and Reports in a real table.
